claims.text: Sustained loading causes progressive plastic deformation in nanoscale HEA multilayer coatings.
Progressive deformation is governed primarily by the accumulation and gradual motion of edge dislocations.
Compositional fluctuations and their associated lattice distortions slow and locally pin edge dislocations at layer interfaces.
Pinned dislocation segments form wavy dislocation lines.
Pinned and wavy dislocations facilitate interface-mediated strain relaxation and localized plasticity over time.
The proposed starting material consists of alternating FCC and BCC HEA layers with coherent or semi-coherent interfaces.
The starting multilayer has inherent compositional complexity and associated lattice distortion.
Room or moderately elevated temperatures can permit creep testing while avoiding diffusion-induced degradation of the nanoscale multilayer.
A constant stress in the elastic-plastic transition regime is an appropriate condition for testing the proposed mechanism.
Alternating layers and coherent interfaces magnify the effects of lattice distortion caused by compositional fluctuations.
The magnified lattice distortion produces localized pinning of edge dislocations.
The random distribution of multiple elements creates severe lattice distortion in the HEA layers.
Severe lattice distortion deflects the cores of predominantly <111>{110} edge dislocations.
Compositional and crystallographic mismatch locally pins dislocations at the interfaces during sustained loading.
Interfacial pinning leads to through-thickness dislocation accumulation and activation of plastic flow along interfaces.
Creep will increase the density of pinned and wavy edge dislocations near layer boundaries relative to the undeformed baseline.
Interfacial dislocation accumulation will accompany progressive plastic strain and local interface shear.
The proposed response will be stronger in multilayers having greater compositional fluctuation.
The mechanism applies only while the nanoscale layered structure is retained without substantial interdiffusion or interface decohesion and before catastrophic failure.

Failure to observe enhanced interfacial pinned or wavy dislocation density, or failure of progressive strain to correlate with interfacial dislocation accumulation, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
